\section{The exact nonlinear heat-kernel action}\label{sec:nonlinear}

Identify $\SUtwo$ with the unit quaternions and $\suTwo$ with pure imaginary
quaternions.  On $\norm a<\pi$,
\[
 \exp a=\left(\cos\norm a,
   \frac{\sin\norm a}{\norm a}a\right).
\]
For a plaquette with oriented link-log inputs $a_1,\ldots,a_4$, define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:X-def}
 X_p(A)=\log\bigl(\exp a_1\exp a_2\exp(-a_3)\exp(-a_4)\bigr).
\end{equation}
Its derivative at the origin is the corresponding row of $d_1\otimes\Id_3$.

Let $p_t$ be the $\SUtwo$ heat kernel for generator $\frac12\Delta$ on the
unit three-sphere.  The rooted-tree-gauge density in logarithmic coordinates
has action, up to an additive constant,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-action}
 S_t(A)=-\sum_{p\in B_2}\log p_t(\exp X_p(A))
        -\sum_{e\notin T}\log j(A_e),
\end{equation}
where $j$ is \eqref{eq:haar-log-density}.  Thus both the non-Abelian plaquette
geometry and the quotient Haar density are included.

Define the convex chart
\begin{equation}\label{eq:chart}
 \cC_r=\left\{A:\norm{E_pA}\le r\text{ for every }p\in B_2\right\},
 \qquad r=10^{-5},
\end{equation}
where $E_p$ extracts the four link variables around $p$ with the direct-sum
Euclidean norm.

\begin{lemma}[Product--log bounds]\label{lem:product-log}
For $2r<1$, put
\begin{align*}
 M_1(r)&=\frac2{1-2r},\\
 M_2(r)&=\frac4{(1-2r)^2}+\frac4{1-2r},\\
 M_3(r)&=\frac{16}{(1-2r)^3}
       +\frac{24}{(1-2r)^2}+\frac8{1-2r}.
\end{align*}
On $\norm{E_pA}\le r$,
\[
 \norm{DX_p}\le M_1,\quad \norm{D^2X_p}\le M_2,\quad
 \norm{D^3X_p}\le M_3,\quad
 \norm{DX_p-d_1|_p}\le M_2r,\quad \norm{X_p}\le2r.
\]
At $r=10^{-5}$ the exact rational majorants satisfy
\[
 M_1<2.001,\qquad M_2<8.01,\qquad M_3<48.1.
\]
\end{lemma}

The proof is in Appendix~\ref{app:heat-kernel}.  Since each link occurs in at
most six plaquettes,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:extraction}
 \sum_p\norm{E_ph}^2\le6\norm h^2.
\end{equation}
It follows that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kappa}
 \norm{DX(A)-D\otimes\Id_3}\le\kappa,\qquad
 \kappa=\sqrt6M_2r<\frac1{1000}.
\end{equation}

\begin{corollary}[Nonlinear curvature injectivity]\label{cor:injectivity}
For $A,A'\in\cC_r$ in tree gauge,
\[
 \norm{X(A)-X(A')}\ge\frac{199}{1000}\norm{A-A'}.
\]
Thus the nonlinear curvature map is injective on $\cC_r$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:cotree-coercivity} gives
$\norm{D(A-A')}\ge\frac15\norm{A-A'}$.  Integrate
$DX-D$ along the segment from $A'$ to $A$ and use \eqref{eq:kappa}.
\end{proof}

The heat-kernel image formula and the elementary Haar density give the
following uniform initializer.

\begin{lemma}[Local heat-kernel and Haar initializer]\label{lem:heat-init}
If $0<t\le10^{-18}$ and $\norm x\le2\cdot10^{-5}$, write
\[
 -t\log p_t(\exp x)=\tfrac12\norm x^2+c_t+q_t(x).
\]
Then
\[
 \norm{Dq_t}\le 2t\norm x,\qquad
 \norm{D^2q_t}\le2t,\qquad \norm{D^3q_t}\le10t.
\]
Moreover, for $\norm A_e\le10^{-5}$,
\[
 \norm{D^2[-t\log j(A_e)]}\le t,\qquad
 \norm{D^3[-t\log j(A_e)]}\le2t.
\]
\end{lemma}

Appendix~\ref{app:heat-kernel} derives the estimates from the paired Poisson
images; the exponential tail is bounded by a rational majorant rather than a
floating underflow.

\begin{proposition}[Certified nonlinear action norm]\label{prop:action-norm}
On $\cC_r$, for all $0<t\le10^{-18}$,
\begin{align}
 \norm{tD^2S_t(A)-H\otimes\Id_3}&<\eta<\frac1{400},\label{eq:eta-bound}\\
 \norm{tD^3S_t(A)}&<\tau<300.\label{eq:tau-bound}
\end{align}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The chain rule, \eqref{eq:extraction}, and Lemmas
\ref{lem:product-log}--\ref{lem:heat-init} give
\begin{align*}
\eta={}&\kappa(2\sqrt{12}+\kappa)
 +2t(\sqrt{12}+\kappa)^2
 +6(2r+4rt)M_2+t,\\
\tau={}&6\left[10tM_1^3+3(1+2t)M_1M_2+(2r+4rt)M_3\right]+2t.
\end{align*}
The exact verifier substitutes $r=1/100000$, $t\le1/10^{18}$,
$\sqrt6<5/2$, and $\sqrt{12}<7/2$.  Fraction comparison gives
$\eta<1/400$ and $\tau<300$.  Appendix~\ref{app:heat-kernel} supplies the
full tensor calculation.
\end{proof}
